title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Glassy but waiting on the CPI set
conditions.summary: Futures are mixed after Monday's big rally, with the Dow helped by sliding oil and the Nasdaq held back by Nvidia worries. October CPI at 7:30 AM CT is the wave everyone is watching.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: Early quotes around 5:30 AM ET: S&P 500 futures about +0.1%, Nasdaq-100 futures about -0.2%, Dow futures about +0.3%, Russell 2000 futures roughly flat.
This follows a huge Monday: the S&P 500 rose about 2.4% for its best day since April, and the Nasdaq gained about 2.7%.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.88%, up about 2 basis points; the dollar index is a touch higher near 101.7.
WTI crude is near $85, down about 2%, and Brent slipped below $90 for the first time since late August as Iran tensions eased.
Gold is down about 1.6% near $4,074, bitcoin is near $74,000 and down about 1.6% over 24 hours, and the VIX sits just under 20.
Asia: Japan's Nikkei jumped about 2.9%, while Hong Kong and Shanghai edged higher. Europe is trading higher.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: October CPI at 7:30 AM CT: consensus +0.3% m/m headline (prior +0.6%) and +0.2% core (prior +0.3%). Some reports say 12-month changes may not be published this month because of last year's shutdown gap.
Fed Governor Waller said in London he backs a 25 basis point hike in December and that 50 should be considered if core CPI runs around 0.3% or higher.
Markets price roughly an 80% chance of a December rate hike.
Fed speakers later: Logan (morning), Schmid at 12:30 PM CT, Bowman at 2:30 PM CT.
The Treasury sells $42 billion of 10-year notes at noon CT. NFIB small business optimism for October held steady.
Tomorrow is Veterans Day: the bond market is closed, stocks are open.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Monday.com shares fell after a third-quarter beat as its retention rate declined.
Quantum Computing Inc. fell about 4% after earnings despite a huge jump in revenue.
Before the open today: D-Wave Quantum, Sea Ltd, Wix, On Holding, Vodafone, Venture Global and Embraer are among the names on the calendar.
After the close: CoreWeave is the big one, with consensus calling for a loss of about $1.45 to $1.53 a share on revenue near $3.5 billion; investors will watch backlog and debt costs.
Also after the close: Rigetti Computing, Petrobras and Ecopetrol.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): up about 1% early — bouncing after Monday's 4% drop on reports its board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged China-linked relationship.
CRWV (CoreWeave): up about 1% to 2% — ahead of its earnings report after the close.
INTC (Intel): down about 2% — chip names cooling after Monday's big semiconductor rally.
MRVL (Marvell): down about 2% — same chip-sector pullback.
MNDY (Monday.com): lower — falling despite an earnings beat as customer retention slipped.
QUBT (Quantum Computing Inc.): about -4% — post-earnings selling despite surging revenue.
Gold miners: down about 0.4% to 1.8% — following gold lower and reversing Monday's gains.
Pre-market quotes are early and thin; movers may shift before the open.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic is reportedly starting its IPO roadshow, with a draft prospectus pointing to a raise of up to about $64 billion, which would be one of the largest IPOs ever.
President Trump said military action against Iran may end fairly soon and delayed further strikes, while keeping the naval blockade; Iran disputed reports of talks.
Russia, Ukraine and the US open trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, the first in nine months.
TSMC said October revenue rose about 60% from a year ago, and China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion.
Wall Street bonuses are on track to rise for a third straight year.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT: October CPI — a core reading at 0.3% or higher could revive talk of a 50 basis point Fed hike.
Noon CT: $42 billion 10-year note auction, with the 10-year yield near 4.88%.
After the close: CoreWeave earnings, a fresh read on AI spending and debt.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November tenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. My co-anchor Gus the wonder dog just shook the sand off his paws and took his seat. Give the Dawn Patrol a big hello, Gus! Let's check the swell. After Monday's gnarly rally, the best day for the S and P five hundred since April, the water is glassy but choppy at the edges. Early quotes show S and P futures up about a tenth of a percent. Nasdaq one hundred futures are down about two tenths. Dow futures are up about three tenths, and small caps are flat. The ten year Treasury yield is near four point eight eight percent, up about two basis points. Oil is sliding about two percent, with crude near eighty five dollars. Brent dipped under ninety for the first time since August as Iran tensions cooled. Gold is down about one and a half percent, bitcoin is near seventy four thousand, and the fear gauge sits just under twenty. Over in Asia, Japan's Nikkei caught a big wave, up almost three percent. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Europe is higher too. Now the wind and weather. The big set rolls in at seven thirty A M Central with the October consumer price index. Forecasters see prices up three tenths of a percent for the month, and core up two tenths. Fed Governor Waller says he backs a quarter point hike in December, and a half point should be on the table if core comes in hot. Markets see about an eighty percent chance of a December hike. On the tide chart, Monday dot com slipped despite an earnings beat as customer retention softened. Tonight, CoreWeave reports after the close, a big test for AI spending and debt. Rigetti and Petrobras report tonight too. In the lineup, Nvidia is paddling back about one percent after a four percent wipeout Monday on reports its board is investigating the C E O. CoreWeave is up one to two percent ahead of earnings. Intel and Marvell are down about two percent as chips cool off. Gold miners are drifting lower. Early quotes are thin, so stay loose. Beach talk: Anthropic is reportedly starting its I P O roadshow, aiming to raise up to about sixty four billion dollars. That's no grommet. And Russia, Ukraine and the United States open talks in Abu Dhabi. Sets to watch: the inflation report at seven thirty, the ten year note auction at noon Central, and CoreWeave tonight. Tomorrow is Veterans Day, so the bond market takes a beach day while stocks stay open. Got a stock, E T F or futures contract on your mind? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
